paragraphs.source_en: Hashiba Hideyoshi sent a secret envoy to Ishikawa Kazumasa, informing him that preparations had been made for Lady Asahi's marriage. This occurred on the fourth day after Hideyoshi had marched out with an army of one hundred thousand to conquer Kii Province—the twenty-fifth day of the third month in the thirteenth year of Tenshō.

units.source_en: Hashiba Hideyoshi sent a secret envoy to Ishikawa Kazumasa, informing him that preparations had been made for Lady Asahi's marriage.

paragraphs.source_en: Hideyoshi had first entered Kishiwada Castle on the twenty-first. He ordered his younger brother, Hashiba Chūnagon Hidenaga, and his nephew, Miyoshi Chūnagon Hidetsugu, to attack Sengokubori, a fortification built by the followers of Negoro-ji; then sent the combined forces of Takayama, Nakagawa, and Tsutsui directly against Negoro-ji, while Hosokawa Tadaoki and Gamō Ujisato were dispatched to strike Shakuzen-ji.

units.source_zh: 秀吉首先于二十一日进入岸和田城，派其弟羽柴中纳言秀长与外甥三好中纳言秀次攻打根来寺徒众所建的千石堀，续派高山、中川、筒井的联军直接攻击根来寺，派细川忠兴、蒲生氏乡袭击积善寺。

paragraphs.source_en: On the twenty-third, Negoro-ji was burned to the ground. On the twenty-fourth, Kokawa-dera too was reduced to a field of ashes.

paragraphs.source_en: Perhaps this was not quite the proper way to handle things! Both the matter of taking Lady Asahi as a bride and Oyoshimaru's first campaign had to be discussed with Hideyoshi; there was therefore no longer any need to conceal them from Ieyasu. In truth, the situation was not so grave: Ieyasu had no intention whatever of fighting Hideyoshi. Kazumasa had initially felt some misgivings on the road, but, certain that he would ultimately obtain Ieyasu's approval, he put his mind at ease.
